source: Let's make a cel-shading 3D game called Gallery. The core loop is paint using a simplified canvas, you're only given 45 seconds, and your canvas you can equip new colors that you've unlocked but can only have 4 available per round. The art you make gets saved and added to a new permanent portrait image in your digital gallery. You can always go up to and inspect these, by walking around in 3D in the gallery then inspecting. The most recent one you make is on a 3D easel at the front of your gallery. Every time you paint a new image with a combination of colors you haven't used before, you get to permanently unlock a new paint color you can use.

answers.ask: Cel-shading is a render style rather than a setting - should the gallery read as a clean white-cube museum, a cosy home studio, or something else?
answers.answer: Make it a clean white-cube museum rendered in cel-shaded 3D, with the easel prominently placed at the front.

answers.ask: How many finished portraits should the gallery be sized to hold before it has to expand?
answers.answer: Size the initial gallery for 12 finished portraits before it expands.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Cel-shading is a render style rather than a setting - should the gallery read as a clean white-cube museum, a cosy home studio, or something else? A: Make it a clean white-cube museum rendered in cel-shaded 3D, with the easel prominently placed at the front.
- [author] scale — Q: How many finished portraits should the gallery be sized to hold before it has to expand? A: Size the initial gallery for 12 finished portraits before it expands.
- [agent_inferred] portrait arrangement — Q: How should twelve portrait positions be distributed in the initial room? A: Use six evenly spaced wall positions on each of the two long side walls.
- [agent_inferred] expansion boundary — Q: Where should the gallery expand after all twelve positions are filled? A: Reserve one clean capacity-gated doorway in the rear wall for a future wing.

## Enriched image prompt
Build Gallery as one clean white-cube museum interior rendered in cel-shaded 3D. Place a prominent 3D easel and simplified painting canvas at the front of the room as the first focal object; this easel displays the player's most recent artwork after painting. Run a clear central walking aisle toward the rear wall. Arrange exactly twelve permanent portrait positions along the two long side walls, six evenly spaced on each side, with enough floor clearance for a player to approach and inspect every image. Keep the white walls, pale floor, crisp outlines, and minimal museum lighting uncluttered so saved artwork supplies the color. Reserve one clean closed expansion doorway in the rear wall for a future gallery wing after all twelve portrait positions are filled.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Entertainment because the 3D space is an indoor gallery walked through to inspect artwork. Simulation is secondary for the timed painting station.

## Shape and preset
Use `interior-single`: the entire initial experience is one enclosed gallery room with no exterior. The matched preset is Indoor Venue.

## Config requirements
Use `social-hub` for the broad central aisle and viewing space. Use `spawn-first-reveal` for a front arrival position aimed directly at the prominent easel. Draw the visible half of `trigger-task`, taken from Simulation's catalogue row, as the easel and painting canvas. Use `gate-progression` for the clean rear expansion doorway that remains closed until twelve portraits fill the room. Use free-text image content for exactly twelve permanent portrait frames, six per long wall.

## Layout requirements
Place one `spawn-first-reveal` SpawnZone at the front entrance, oriented toward the easel. Place one `trigger-task` TriggerZone at the painting canvas. Place twelve free-text TriggerZones, one inspect point in front of each permanent portrait position. Painting time, four equipped colors, color unlocks, artwork saving, and portrait-image updates are mechanics.

## Layout components
The room contains one front entrance, one focal easel, one painting canvas, one central aisle, twelve wall portraits, and one rear expansion threshold. Six portraits line each long side wall with consistent spacing and clear inspection floor. The white-cube walls fully enclose the initial gallery. Compose the view from the entrance so the easel dominates the foreground, portrait rows recede along both sides, and the rear doorway closes the axis.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the cel-shaded white-cube presentation and easel-first composition lead, while the one-room circulation plan is simple.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is small because the easel, painting controls, and all twelve portrait inspection points must remain legible. The theme is a clean white-cube museum rendered in cel-shaded 3D. The pipeline uses `P0`: this is one interior-only single-surface room, and the future expansion wing is not generated in the initial build.
